CoALA (Sumers et al., TMLR): language agents framed as modular memory (incl. procedural), structured action space, generalized decision cycle — the cognitive-architecture backbone of the hybrid.
SmartPlay (Microsoft): LLM-as-agent benchmark over 6 games diagnosing capabilities (planning ahead, spatial reasoning, learning from history); roadmap for exposing LLM agent capability gaps.

CodeAct (ICML 2024): executable code actions up to 20% higher success than JSON/text baselines across 17 LLMs; interpreter loop enables self-debug.
Kambhampati et al., 'Position: LLMs Can't Plan, But Can Help Planning in LLM-Modulo Frameworks' (ICML 2024) abstract: LLMs as knowledge/model generators inside loops with external sound verifiers.

'Agents Thinking Fast and Slow: A Talker-Reasoner Architecture' (Christakopoulou, Mourad, Mataric, 2024): Talker (System 1, fast conversational) + Reasoner (System 2, planning/tools/actions); cites modularity and decreased latency.
BALROG (ICLR 2025): agentic LLM/VLM benchmark on games (NetHack tier hardest); models get partial success on easy games and 'struggle significantly' on hard ones; vision input can hurt vs text-only.

DPT-Agent (ACL 2025 main): System 1 = FSM + code-as-policy for fast controllable decisions, System 2 = LLM with Theory of Mind and asynchronous reflection; claims first autonomous success at real-time simultaneous human-AI collaboration.

2025 RAMP/NSAM(+p): integrates RL policies, numeric action-model learning, and planning in Minecraft; RAMP solves more problems and finds more efficient plans than several RL baselines — recent hybrid convergence of trained skills under a symbolic planner.

PORTAL paper (Xu et al. 2025) abstract: LLMs generate 'behavior trees represented in domain-specific language (DSL)', hybrid rule+neural nodes, validated across thousands of FPS games; policies 'instantaneously deployable, human-interpretable'.

MAST (UC Berkeley): taxonomy of 14 LLM agent-system failure modes in 3 categories (system design, inter-agent misalignment, task verification) from 1,600+ traces — cited to argue fewer architectural layers means fewer failure classes.
SkillWeaver 2025: agents synthesizing skills as APIs gain 31.8% (WebArena) / 39.8% (real sites); skills transfer to weaker agents up to 54.3%.
